control_flow: followInTheDark: if the right light reads below 60, follow the line in the dark; else avoid walls.
Following the line in the dark: line below 90 curves left, else line above 95 curves right, else avoid walls.

avoidWalls: if the left light reads below 70, turn away from a side obstacle (left → turn right 20°, else right → turn left 20°), else drive in the dark; if the left light is bright, drive in the dark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light reads below 70, drive forward at 30 %; else check for a wall.
stopAtWall: if something is ahead, stop; else follow the line.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black curve left (10/40), else curve right (40/10).

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line, and keep following it when the line goes into a dark tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black (10 % left, 40 % right) and curves right on the floor (40 % left, 10 % right).
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a line in bright light, in the open.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in the light
assumptions: The end of the line is where it should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end.

scenarios.coded_response: Below 60 % on the right light it follows the line with faster curves (15/35 and 35/15); on a brief in-between reading and in the dim band it drives straight forward at 30 %.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line on a bright floor that runs on into a tunnel, and a goal is in the dark inside it.
scenarios.trigger: The light on the robot falls as it goes under the roof; the line continues.
scenarios.title: Follows the line into a dark tunnel
assumptions: The goal is in the dark part of the tunnel.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It keeps following the line into the dark and gets to the goal inside the tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops and stays stopped while the wall is ahead.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light, with a wall across the line ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall in the light
assumptions: You didn't say it, but the program is built to stop when something is ahead in the light.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

scenarios.coded_response: It turns right 20° when something is on its left, turns left 20° when something is on its right, otherwise drives forward.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line into a tunnel that bends, so the tunnel's wall comes in front of its left or right side.
scenarios.trigger: In the dark it checks its side obstacle sensors.
scenarios.title: Turns away from a tunnel wall in the dark
assumptions: The program should get through the bend without bumping the tunnel's wall.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns away from the tunnel wall and gets through the bend without bumping.

uncertainties: In the dark the robot only reaches its side-obstacle check through a brief in-between reading of the line, so turning away from a tunnel wall may happen only now and then.
You said follow the line in the dark, but on a plain floor the program curves right and circles, so it needs a line to get anywhere.
The program checks the right light sensor first: below 60 it follows the line, at 60 or more it goes to avoid walls.
